subject.title: feat: add readiness conditions and providers

question: Should OpenClaw V1 permanently expose the public `api.registerReadinessCriterion` Plugin SDK contract and the `gateway.readiness` selection configuration, or should plugin-provided readiness be deferred while core-only readiness lands first?
rationale: The choice defines a supported external Plugin SDK and configuration compatibility contract; it cannot be resolved safely as a mechanical review fix.

options.title: Approve the V1 plugin contract
options.body: Adopt the public readiness callback and operator-selection identifiers, then require exact-head fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Land core-only readiness first
options.body: Keep canonical Gateway readiness and core-owned conditions, but remove or defer public plugin registration until maintainers choose the durable SDK shape.

options.title: Pause the feature direction
options.body: Keep the PR open only if maintainers intend to continue RFC-level design before committing this API surface.

recommendation.title: Approve the V1 plugin contract
recommendation.body: Adopt the public readiness callback and operator-selection identifiers, then require exact-head fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: A public Plugin SDK and operator configuration contract requires repository-level product direction; no more specific current-main owner could be established from the available read-only context.
